title: Surgical agentlet: AutoFlow for on-call playbook execution and contextual helpers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight 'agentlet' that executes compact, idempotent runbook steps (AutoFlow) in the on-call flow with contextual hints and safety rails. The agentlet should: 1) interpret a runbook task graph entry, 2) surface only the minimal operator UI/actions for that step, 3) execute safe, pre-approved commands via the operator backend, and 4) emit structured telemetry for audit and rollback.

Why this work: current runbook executions require full runbook editors or manual orchestration. For common recurring ops tasks (rotate keys, restart shard, boost capacity), on-call engineers need a fast, low-friction surface that reduces cognitive load and mistakes while preserving traceability. This ticket scopes the first iteration of AutoFlow agentlets with a strong emphasis on constraints and safety.

Non-goals: full visual runbook editor, arbitrary script execution, or replacing the existing runbook DSL. This is an execution path optimized for speed and safety during incidents and routine maintenance.
acceptance_criteria: Agentlet can be invoked from Console quick-actions and the ops CLI with a task key and context
Each agentlet step declares required inputs and allowed side-effects; runtime enforces a whitelist of actions
All agentlet executions produce an immutable audit record (actor, inputs, outputs, exit code, artifacts) stored in the ops audit log
Default safety timeout and a reversible flag for destructive ops; destructive steps require 2-step confirmation or approval from an oncall lead
End-to-end e2e test simulating restart and KV cache flush demonstrating idempotency and telemetry emission
implementation_notes:
Planned as a two-component system: (A) small stateless agentlet runner service that receives a task payload and executes pre-approved action handlers; (B) a registry of handlers (restart-service, rotate-kms-key, scale-gpu-pool, flush-kv-cache) implemented as idempotent functions in the operator backend. Execution flow: Console/CLI -> broker -> runner -> handler -> event/audit. Use existing ops-auth tokens and scoping; do not add new long-lived credentials. Prefer grpc for runner<->handler calls to reduce latency.

Telemetry: add event types agentlet.start, agentlet.step.complete, agentlet.step.fail, agentlet.finish with span IDs to link to traces. Leverage existing tracing headers so incidents can jump from a failed agentlet execution to the request trace.

Safety: implement strict handler whitelist per environment, require feature-flag for destructive handlers, and include 'dry-run' mode for all agentlets.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged beta for internal SREs, then opt-in for a small set of product engineers, then gradual enable for on-call via Console toggles.

Dependencies: requires ops-auth scope extension (ENG-871200) and audit-log retention schema changes (ENG-832415).
notes: Trade-offs considered: embedding a Lua-like sandbox in the runner vs. a fixed handler registry. We chose fixed registry for safety and simpler review paths.
Kernel scheduling impact: the restart-service handler will call the same rolling restart API used by Dedicated; coordinate with infra team for throttling to avoid overload.
Fallback: when runner is unavailable, Console will surface a read-only set of suggested manual steps with links to runbooks and a one-click create incident action.

2026-03-08 - Marcus Nguyen: Spike completed. Implemented a PoC runner that supports restart-service and dry-run. Observed ~120ms median latency for handler calls in our dev cluster. Added grpc stub and tracing propagation.

2026-03-10 - Lila Romero (SRE): Reviewed PoC. Safety concerns about restart concurrency. Requested per-handler concurrency limits and global rate limiter. Also requested audit schema to include human-acknowledgement field.
2026-03-12 - Marcus Nguyen: Added concurrency limiter and feature-flag gates for destructive handlers. Updated PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runbooks/pull/429. Running manual tests on staging.
